close_reason: Top-level README CRL example now explicitly notes that 'crl' Cargo feature is required ('pkix-chain = { version = "0.2", features = ["crl"] }'). Mirrors the documentation pattern already used in the per-crate READMEs.
description:
## Anchor
Pass-2 commit e586bc49 rewrote the top-level README quick-start examples to fix the broken pre-pass-1 examples (PKIX-qwzx.2, PKIX-qwzx.6).

## Finding
README.md:46-48 says:
```toml
[dependencies]
pkix-chain = "0.2"
```

README.md:74-81 then shows a CRL example using `pkix_chain::CrlChecker`. But pkix-chain/Cargo.toml gates `CrlChecker` re-export behind `features = ["crl"]` (lines 16, 41-42). With the dependency line as written, `use pkix_chain::CrlChecker` does not resolve.

Reproduced: `cargo build` against pkix-chain (default features) with the literal README CRL example body fails with E0432 (unresolved import). Adding `features = ["crl"]` to the dependency line resolves it.

## Severity
P3 / opinion. The first example (NoRevocation) compiles. The CRL example was the entire purpose of PKIX-qwzx.6 — that issue closed correctly on the API surface (Result-returning new()) but the broader compilability issue is that the README still does not tell the reader they need features = ["crl"].

## Fix
One-line update to README.md:46-48 — change `pkix-chain = "0.2"` to `pkix-chain = { version = "0.2", features = ["crl"] }` for the CRL example, OR add a sentence above the CRL example saying "Enable the `crl` feature."

## Why this is P3 not higher
- The first example (the more-prominent quick-start) compiles fine with default features.
- This is documentation, not behavior.
- A sophisticated reader will notice the cfg-gated re-export from rustdoc and figure it out.

## Pass-2 attribution
Pass-2 closure of PKIX-qwzx.6 ("CRL example uses pre-P3 CrlChecker::new signature") fixed the new() signature change but did not surface the feature-flag requirement.
title: P3: top-level README CRL example silently requires features=["crl"]
